neighbours.label: a determiner or possessive (my, your, the, any) opening the object right after a transitive verb ('eat my supper', 'receive your jewelry')
fire: After the long hike we sat down and ate our sandwiches.
Please wash your hands before touching the bread.
You can return your order within thirty days.
Grandpa likes to polish his boots every Sunday.
Do not feed any animals you meet on the trail.
First, unpack the box and charge your new phone.
She opened her letter slowly at the kitchen table.
Before bed the children brush their teeth and read.
quiet: After the long hike we sat down in our tent to rest.
Please stay with your group near the bakery.
You can find the receipt in your email within the hour.
Grandpa likes to sit on his porch every Sunday.
Do not walk off the path for any reason on the trail.
First, look inside the box for a short manual.
She sat by her window slowly at the kitchen table.
Before bed the children sit in their room and read.

notes: Card: 'take My offering', 'eat my supper', 'receive your jewelry', 'attach your seat', 'eat any'. Near misses put the same determiners after prepositions.
